paper.core_task: Enhancing long-context modeling in state space models with integrated internal and external memory

contributions.name: Chunk-wise internal memory mechanism for Mamba-based SSMs
contributions.author_claim_text: We introduce a chunk-wise long-term memory mechanism for Mamba-based SSMs.
contributions.description: An architectural enhancement that partitions input sequences into chunks to mitigate information forgetting and improve in-sequence recall over long distances.

contributions.name: Pre-training methodology to integrate static external knowledge
contributions.author_claim_text: We propose a novel pre-training methodology to deeply integrate a static, pre-encoded external knowledge base into the model's learning process.
contributions.description: A joint pre-training method that fuses pre-encoded external knowledge (e.g., embeddings) directly into the model's architecture, avoiding raw text concatenation.

contributions.name: Plastic Unified Memory Network architecture and training system
contributions.author_claim_text: We combine these advancements in our Plastic Unified Memory Network (PUM-Net).
contributions.description: A unified architecture combining dynamic internal and static external memory with staged parallel computation for training and inference.

novelty_claims.text: Despite the emphasis on external memory integration, the paper does not directly compare PUM-Net with established RAG methods like REALM or RETRO.
The contribution lies in the integration of a dual-memory system into SSMs, which is novel in scope.
